messages:
sam: Quick question re: audit exports — legal asked for last 90d of 'who did X' but we can't include PII. Our exports currently include user_id and session_id. Can we ship exports with pseudonymized IDs that are reversible only with an approval flow?

natalie: Short answer: yes, but we need an approval + KMS-wrapped mapping and strict logging. Do we already have a stable `user_hash` in the audit schema or are we relying on raw user_id?

sam: I checked — audit_events view has `user_id`, `user_email` (nullable), and `user_hash`. The ad-hoc CSV job still SELECTs `user_id` if present. Current snippet we use:```sql
SELECT timestamp, action, user_id, session_id, details
FROM audit_events
WHERE ts >= {{from}} AND ts < {{to}}
```

ryan: We can change the generator to emit `pseudonym = hmac_sha256(kms_key_alias, user_id)` and drop plain `user_id` from blobs. For reversible exports, we can include an `encrypted_reid_token` in S3 object metadata (encrypted with KMS). De-anonymization would require a console-approved flow that creates a temporary IAM role and logs the whole operation.

jules: Legal wants a sealed unmasking process: only on subpoena or signed request, must have case id, two signatories from Legal + one from SecOps to approve, and we log the unmask action (who, why, TTL). Also please don't include emails in exports under any pseudonymized flow.

natalie: Agreed. Runbook updates needed. Also retention question: exports default to 30d in S3 lifecycle; legal sometimes asks for 90d for investigations. Current s3 path pattern: `s3://audit-exports/prod/YYYY/MM/DD/<export-id>.parquet`. Can we gate longer retention by case-id label?

sam: Parquet is cleaner for schema, but some analysts prefer TSV for quick grep. Could produce both or emit a small manifest. Manifest example: {schema_version: 3, format: parquet, pseudonym: reversible} — maybe include as `manifest.json` alongside the object.

security-bot: audit-export v3 job queued by @audit-service. Link: https://ci.internal/jobs/456 — note: exports that use reversible pseudonymization set header `x-redwood-pseudonym-kms-id`.

ryan: Implementation plan: 1) change export generator to select `user_hash` as primary id and remove `user_email`/`user_id` from payload by default; 2) if `--reversible` flag passed, add `encrypted_reid_token` to object metadata and write a row to `audit_reid_requests` with requestor, case_id, approvers, TTL; 3) support manifest with `schema_v` and `format`. I'll open a PR and a migration script for the export pipeline.

sam: Who can run ad-hoc exports today? I thought infra and SecOps only. Need to lock this down so Legal can't accidentally run exports without approval.

natalie: ACL today: `infra:export`, `security:export` (full), `legal:export-read` (read only). We'll add `legal:export-request` that triggers the approval flow rather than direct run. Jules to be final sign-off.

jules: I'll draft acceptance criteria for the runbook: required fields (case_id, justification, approvers), retention instructions, and an audit checklist. Send me the PR link and I'll review.

sam: I'll create the runbook PR. Sample CLI usage to include in docs:```bash
audit-export --from 2026-02-01 --to 2026-03-31 --pseudonym reversible --format parquet --case-id CASE-123
```

audit-service: Noted. We'll add a console "request unmask" flow that routes to SecOps for approval and creates the `audit_reid_requests` record. ETA for endpoint + UI: ~2w.

natalie: Quick crypto check — if we rotate the KMS key, will pseudonym values change? We need deterministic mapping across rotations unless we intentionally rekey.

ryan: We'll use KMS HMAC/deterministic HMAC with a stable key alias. If a rekey is performed, mapping will change; we'll provide an opt-in re-identify job that can map old pseudonyms to new ones under controlled conditions.

sam: Great. I'll open tickets for: runbook PR, ACL changes, export-generator PR, and a short e2e test that validates `encrypted_reid_token` appears only after approval. Thanks all — cc @natalie for review.
